why_relevant: Author of the 18-book Epitome of Histories, whose book XIV, ch. XVII carries the one extended Byzantine chronicle account of Muhammad's origin (epilepsy, a monk, a widow, a claim to Gabriel's visions).
fame: Known to scholars as a Byzantine historian and canonist/commentator; the Epitome is a standard source for Byzantine history from Creation to 1118. His Islam passage is not widely cited (not verified). Also credited with commentaries and canonical works.
orthodox_status: theologian / historian (monk and canonist; not canonized; within the Orthodox Church of his time)

born: c. 1130 (Wikipedia, en: 'possibly c. 1130'; UNVERIFIED against a primary source)
died: unknown; alive after c. 1164 (imprisonment noted in Wikipedia, en; UNVERIFIED)
role_place: Constantinople; imperial secretary (grammatikos) under Manuel I Komnenos; imprisoned and partly blinded after a conspiracy; wrote his Annales in prison or afterwards.
why_relevant: His Annales (Pars IV, Bonn 1836, pp. 513-514) include a doctrinal account of Muhammad: a false prophet, a borrowed 'religion' from Jews, Arians and Nestorians, circumcision kept but the Sabbath dropped, Qur'anic paradise rivers, the 'shadow of Christ' crucified, and a denial that Christ called himself God.
fame: Known to scholars as a Byzantine chronicler and theologian (and a critic of Manuel I); his Muhammad account is not widely cited (not verified). The identification with Michael Sikidites, a heresy suspect c. 1200, is a modern hypothesis (Kresten), not established.
orthodox_status: theologian / historian (not canonized; his orthodoxy was questioned in later sources only through a disputed identification with Sikidites)

born: c. 1155, Chonae (Wikipedia, en; UNVERIFIED against a primary source)
role_place: Constantinople; imperial official (judge of the velum, city administration) who wrote the History from 1118 to 1206/1207, in exile after 1204.
why_relevant: His History (Bonn 1835, book VII on Manuel I) reports two Manuel-era controversies: the anathema against 'the God of Muhammad' in the catechetical tablet, which Manuel ordered removed, and a decree defending the Muslim God; Choniates calls Muhammad's teaching 'nonsense' and 'demonic'.
fame: Major Byzantine historian (also the Thesaurus of orthodox faith, covered by another pack). The Manuel-era anathema story is discussed in the literature (G. L. Hanson, 'Manuel I Komnenos and the God of Muhammad'; cited by a secondary search result, not read in this pass).
orthodox_status: theologian / historian (not canonized; Orthodox writer of the Latin-occupation era)

fame: Known for the Roman History and for the controversy with Gregory Palamas; not known for statements on Islam (to be verified).
orthodox_status: theologian / historian (Orthodox, anti-Palamite opponent; not canonized)

role_place: Athens and the Peloponnese; historian of the Ottomans, Histories (Apodeixeis historion) in ten books, Bekker's edition (Bonn 1843).
why_relevant: TWO PASSAGES: the Muslim lawgiver 'Mechmetes' (son of Ali, persuasion first) and the pilgrimage to his tomb with the Alkoran and the immortality of the soul (Bekker 1843, Book III pp. 121, 126). Chalkokondyles reports these as 'it is said' and calls the suspended tomb incredible.
fame: Known as the principal Greek historian of the Ottomans; his account of Islam is cited in the literature (not checked in this pass).
